architecture.combination: OR for crash-management eligibility; detectors developed and scored independently

goal: Causally identify destructive deterioration early enough to preserve a material fraction of subsequent crash loss without frequent false exits.
engineering_benchmark: 50_PERCENT_LOSS_SAVED is a major success benchmark, not a fitting target and not a requirement for every episode.
fitness: classification quality, detection delay, false-alert episodes, temporal stability; portfolio CAGR/wealth prohibited from fitting

detector_A.design: rare high-specificity shock declaration; short confirmation allowed

detector_B.design: slower confirmation accepted; persistence and failed recovery emphasized over shock magnitude

controls.2015: elevated correction / hard control; may enter warning state but should not automatically become systemic crash
controls.ordinary_stress: all evaluable non-crash history contributes to false-alert burden

timing: completed information through t can authorize action no earlier than next tradable session; OFR retains two-business-day lag

validation.portfolio_diagnostic_after_classifier_fr: simulate exit-at-next-session and report fraction of baseline crash loss avoided, including 50% benchmark; do not use this to choose detector parameters

development_evidence.consumed67: diagnostic only after detector freeze; never parameter fitness

search: transparent sparse rules first; bounded search only; no unconstrained GA
stop_rule: If neither detector shows out-of-sample discrimination with manageable false-alert burden, do not optimize portfolio exits to rescue it.
